lines: Nearly every banana here is a clone, and a fungus is coming for it.
They're all Cavendish, copies of one plant grown from its offshoots, with no seeds. So what kills one can kill them all.
It's happened before. In the 1950s a soil fungus wiped out the banana America ate, the Gros Michel, so growers switched to Cavendish.
Now a new strain is killing Cavendish. There's no cure, and it can sit in the soil for decades.
Now it's in Ecuador, the biggest exporter of all, and this time there's no banana to switch to.
